newsitem.title: USA: Opening arguments begin in O.J. Simpson trial.
newsitem.headline: Opening arguments begin in O.J. Simpson trial.

text.p: Opening arguments began Wednesday in the O.J. Simpson civil trial with an attorney vowing to prove that the former football star committed a brutal double-murder.

In an impassioned presentation to the jury, Daniel Petrocelli, a lawyer for the family of murder victim Ronald Goldman, said that Goldman "died with his eyes open" and saw the man who killed him and his friend, Nicole Brown Simpson.
"We will prove to you that Ronald Goldman and Nicole Brown Simpson died at the hands of the defendant, Orenthal James Simpson," Petrocelli told the jurors in the crowded courtroom.
Simpson, who was acquitted of murder charges on Oct. 3, 1995, is on trial in civil court in a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the victims' families.

As the trial moved into high gear after a month of jury selection, Petrocelli alleged that Simpson killed Goldman to eliminate a witness to an earlier fatal attack on Simpson's ex-wife Nicole. He portrayed Goldman as a hero who "might have run" but instead stayed to face down the killer outside Nicole Brown Simpson's Brentwood townhouse.
"In the last furious moments of his life, Ron Goldman saw through his eyes the man who killed his friend Nicole and took his young life away, the man who sits in this courtroom," Petrocelli said.
